sections.h2: Where is St. George, Louisiana, and why is it unusual?
sections.html:
St. George is a city in East Baton Rouge Parish, in the southeast part of the parish, and it is the newest incorporated city in Louisiana. Voters approved it in an election on October 12, 2019, and it covers about 60 square miles.

The path to being recognized was long. A legal action was filed in the 19th Judicial District Court on November 4, 2019, and the district court and the First Circuit Court of Appeal ruled against the incorporation. On April 26, 2024, the Louisiana Supreme Court reversed those rulings in a 4 to 3 decision, according to Wikipedia's summary of the case.

For a seller this history matters in a practical way. The property did not move, but the office that handles permits, code enforcement and zoning for the address changed from the parish to the city, and that shows up in the paper trail behind a house.

The city is run under the Lawrason Act, the state law for most Louisiana municipalities, and its own site describes it as being in the southeast corner of East Baton Rouge Parish.

sections.h2: What areas and roads define St. George?
sections.html:
The areas usually named for St. George are Inniswold, Oak Hills Place, Old Jefferson, Shenandoah, Village St. George and Westminster. The main roads are Interstate 10, U.S. Highway 61, Jefferson Highway and Louisiana Highway 30, which is Nicholson Drive.

Public schools are part of the East Baton Rouge Parish School System, because the new city did not create a separate district. A buyer comparing your house with others will usually ask which subdivision it sits in, how old it is and which side of the highway it is on, so those are the details worth having ready.

sections.h2: Who issues building permits for a house in St. George?
sections.html:
The City of St. George issues permits for work done on or after its permit system began, and applications submitted before October 16, 2024 were handled by East Baton Rouge Parish. That date is printed on the city's building permits page, and it tells you which office to ask when you want the history of a roof, an addition or a pool.

The city says permits are required for most construction, alterations and repairs. Its residential list includes:

  • new construction, additions and remodels;
  • accessory buildings over 200 square feet, or any size in a flood zone;
  • portable accessory structures over 120 square feet;
  • swimming pools, fences and generators;
  • demolitions and electrical, mechanical or plumbing work.

Inspections are requested through the city's online permitting portal, and the city asks that work be complete and accessible before an inspector is called. Unpermitted work can be reported to the city's enforcement address. Sewer tie-in permits for new construction still come from East Baton Rouge Parish Subdivision Engineering.

If you finished a garage conversion or a shed without a permit, a cash buyer who purchases as-is can often take the house without making you pull permits first. A traditional buyer's lender and inspector are more likely to ask for them.

sections.h2: What does flood history mean for selling in St. George?
sections.html:
Flood history is one of the first things a buyer asks about in this part of East Baton Rouge Parish. The Governor's office estimated in a September 2016 report that about 41,000 of the parish's 189,353 housing units flooded in August 2016.

FEMA reported in 2018 that more than half of the homes and businesses damaged in the August 2016 floods were in moderate or low risk areas. In plain terms, a house outside the mapped high-risk zone can still have taken water, so buyers tend to ask for the full story instead of relying on the map.

If your house flooded, gather what you have: repair invoices, permits, any elevation certificate and your flood insurance history. The city's note that accessory buildings of any size need a permit in a flood zone is another reason to check old work before you list.

  • Write down the dates of any water in the house and what was replaced.
  • Keep contractor invoices and permit numbers together.
  • Ask your insurer for a copy of your policy history.

sections.h2: How are property taxes billed on a St. George house?
sections.html:
The East Baton Rouge Parish Sheriff is the tax collector. Notices are generally mailed in the last week of November, taxes are due December 31 and interest runs at 1% per month, according to the sheriff's tax page.

If taxes remain unpaid after January 31, a $2.00 collection fee applies and the property can be advertised for a tax sale, with certified-notice and advertising costs added. The sheriff's page listed a 2026 tax lien auction on July 8. The Assessor's office assesses as of January 1, and the tax roll is open for public inspection for 15 days between August 15 and September 15.

You can pay in person at 222 Saint Louis Street, Room 238, in Baton Rouge, on weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., or call the Sheriff's tax office at (225) 389-4810. Louisiana's House Fiscal Division says the homestead exemption covers $75,000 of fair market value, and that an owner of property sold at tax sale has three years to redeem it.

sections.h2: How does a house sale work in St. George, Louisiana?
sections.html:
A sale of a house in St. George follows Louisiana's civil law rules, so the deed is an act of sale signed before a notary, and it is then recorded in the East Baton Rouge Parish conveyance records. The Civil Code says a transfer of immovable property must be made by authentic act or by act under private signature.

Recording matters because a transfer does not bind third persons until it is filed in the conveyance records of the parish where the property sits. State law also requires the filed act to name the person responsible for property taxes and an address for tax notices (La. R.S. 9:2721).

The steps in a typical sale look like this:

  1. Agree on a price and sign a purchase agreement.
  2. Order title work and a mortgage certificate so any liens appear.
  3. Pay off any mortgage or past-due tax from the proceeds.
  4. Sign the act of sale before a notary and record it.

A cash purchase shortens the lender portion. It does not remove title work, so unpaid tax or an open mortgage is cleared at the table either way. A tax bill that is only a few weeks late is far easier to handle than one that has been advertised for sale.

sections.h2: What do sellers in St. George usually run into?
sections.html:
Sellers here most often face three things: records split between the parish and the city, flood questions and tax timing. None of them blocks a sale, but each one slows a listing if you wait to deal with it.

  • Permit records for older work sit with East Baton Rouge Parish, newer ones with the city.
  • Flood damage history, repairs and insurance need clear answers.
  • The December 31 tax date and January 31 fee date can fall in the middle of a sale.
  • Inherited houses may need a succession before anyone can sign a deed.

A cash offer fits when the house needs work, the owner is out of town or the paperwork is messy. It is not the best route for every house. A well-kept home in a popular subdivision may do well on the open market, and we would rather you compare than guess.

faqs.q: Is St. George a real city or part of Baton Rouge?
faqs.a: St. George is its own city inside East Baton Rouge Parish. Voters approved it on October 12, 2019, and the Louisiana Supreme Court upheld the incorporation on April 26, 2024.

faqs.q: Who do I pay property tax to if I own a house in St. George?
faqs.a: You pay the East Baton Rouge Parish Sheriff, who serves as tax collector. Taxes are due December 31 and carry 1% monthly interest after that.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit record to sell my house in St. George?
faqs.a: No permit record is required to sign a sale, but buyers and lenders often ask for one. Permits before October 16, 2024 sit with East Baton Rouge Parish, and later ones with the City of St. George.

faqs.q: Can I sell a flooded house in St. George as-is?
faqs.a: Yes, an as-is sale is possible. Keep your repair records and flood insurance history ready, because buyers will ask about the August 2016 floods and any later water.

faqs.q: Where is a St. George house sale recorded?
faqs.a: The act of sale is recorded in the East Baton Rouge Parish conveyance records. Recording makes the transfer effective against third persons.
